question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 3, 2 and 6 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do twice the same work, working together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rates: A = 1/3, B = 1/2, C = 1/6

Total rate = 1/3 + 1/2 + 1/6 = 1 work/day

Time for 1 work = 1 day

For 2 works ⇒ 2 × 1 = 2 days

**∴ Answer = 2 days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A = 3 days, B = 2 days, C = 6 days

**Formula used:**

Total rate = sum of individual rates

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total work = 6 units

⇒ Efficiency = 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 units/day

⇒ Time for 1 work = 6 ÷ 6 = 1 day

⇒ Time for 2 works = 2 × 1 = 2 days

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work Rate

LCM Method

Take LCM of days as total work

Scaling

Time increases proportionally with work
